messages:
liz-sales: Heads-up — BankCo POC can't complete calls when their app hits the private VPC endpoint. They're seeing SSL errors + intermittent 504s from our side. Can we triage?
omar-se: Share the client logs and which host they resolve to pls. Quick question: are they using a private hosted zone?
liz-sales: Error copy from their app: 'error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:tlsv1 alert protocol version' then curl shows 'Connection reset by peer' — DNS resolves to internal IP 172.31.45.7.
nina-sre: That TLS alert usually indicates the server closed the connection during negotiation. Could be TLS interception, plain HTTP on 443, or a mismatch in SNI. Are we expecting mutual TLS for this POC?
omar-se: We're using our POC Private endpoint (no mTLS by default). Customer asked for private endpoint in their VPC with an ENI. We expect standard TLS to our cert.
lev-net: Checklist: SG inbound on ENI for 443 from app SG, route table local to the ENI, and no NACL dropping ephemeral ports. Also verify their DNS isn't returning the wrong target via a global resolver cache.
tom-eng: Can someone run `openssl s_client -connect 172.31.45.7:443 -servername api.private.bankco.internal -debug` and paste output? If it's a proxy returning HTML, that'll show immediately.
bankco-infra (posted by customer): Output: 
```
CONNECTED(00000005)
139...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:ssl/record/ssl3_read_bytes.c:1471:
---
no peer certificate available
```
nina-sre: "no peer certificate" + handshake failure points to a middlebox terminating TLS and not forwarding certs. Do they have TLS inspection or a perimeter proxy?
bankco-security (customer): We do have a proxy that does TLS inspection for egress. We thought that should be fine.
omar-se: If their proxy is resigning certs, the client will see our cert replaced. For our endpoint we expect the TCP/TLS flow to go end-to-end. Two options: allowlist this destination so inspection is bypassed, or they add our CA to their proxy trust store (less preferred for short-term POC).
lev-net: Also note: if their proxy performs SNI rewriting or drops unknown SNI, it may reset. Can they confirm the proxy forwards SNI?
bankco-infra: We'll check. Also curious what IPs you require open egress to — security asking for a minimal allowlist.
tom-eng: For POC we can provide a small set of egress IPs (PEER-POC: 52.40.120.9, 52.40.120.10, 52.40.120.11). They should allow outbound 443 and permit OCSP/CRL checks to port 80/443 to common CAs if proxy terminates TLS.
nina-sre: Additional quick tests: 1) Run `curl --resolve "api.private.bankco.internal:443:172.31.45.7" -v https://api.private.bankco.internal/health` from their app host to bypass DNS. 2) Run `tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/cap.pcap port 443` and share.
org-bot: POC ticket created: POC-5582 assigned to tom-eng and nina-sre, due 2026-04-04.
bankco-infra: We ran the curl with --resolve — it shows HTTP/1.1 200 OK when we skip our corporate proxy. But when route goes through default egress it fails.
lev-net: That confirms it's the egress proxy. Next steps for BankCo: 1) create an allowlist exception for api.private.bankco.internal so TLS is not intercepted OR 2) add our CA to proxy trust and ensure SNI is forwarded. Also confirm SG rules and NACLs.
omar-se: If they can't change proxy rules, we can stand up a short-lived non-TLS listener on a test port to validate routing only (no certs). If that works, it's network-only and we can iterate on TLS config.
tom-eng: I'll deploy a debug listener returning 200 on port 8443 (no TLS) for 1 hour. ETA 90 mins. Post results here.
bankco-security: We'll ask infra to add an exception for the POC hostname; security to approve within 4 hours. We'll report back.
liz-sales: Thanks team. Can we also supply a short FAQ for customers re: Private endpoints (DNS, TLS inspection, allowlists, OCSP) so security teams know what to expect?
nina-sre: Yes — I'll draft a short checklist and drop it in the POC template repo after this incident.

Final update 5h later from customer: security approved exception, turned off TLS inspection for the hostname, re-ran curl health check, now returns 200 and the app completed POC workflows. We'll follow up with a post-mortem and checklist. :white_check_mark:
